name: reanimen
summary: a script-to-video editor built around a black canvas, sourced images and GIFs, word-synced captions, and narration. edit each scene, optionally convert the voice locally with RVC, then render an MP4 through remotion.
problem: Build narrated videos from a script using a deliberately simple black canvas, sourced images and GIF cutaways, and captions synchronized to the spoken words.
highlights: Scene-based editing: Build scenes from a script, then adjust layouts, cuts, motion, caption position, and visual style individually.
Media sourcing: Derive search terms from the narration and find images or GIFs through media providers, retaining attribution in project data.
Narration & rendering: Generate scene narration with word boundaries for captions, optionally convert its voice through RVC, and render an MP4 with Remotion.

media.caption: Running Reanimen editor with its bundled sample script and scene controls, before narration or rendering.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Paste the script and build scenes.
- Review sourced images and GIFs.
- Generate narration and tune scene presentation.
- Render and download the finished MP4.

sections.heading: Under the hood
sections.body: The editor connects Remotion rendering with a Python Edge-TTS bridge. Optional local RVC conversion preserves timing, while cached audio avoids unnecessary regeneration.

sections.heading: Scope & current state
sections.body: Edge-TTS and media search require online services; optional RVC inference runs locally. Sourced media still needs a rights review before publication.
